import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1038

*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
 - [Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025
  (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
-/

open scoped Real ENNReal
open MeasureTheory

namespace Erdos1038

/-- What is the infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such
that all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 28]
theorem erdos_1038.parts.i (n : ℕ) : answer(sorry) =
    ⨅ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧ f ≠ 1 ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1} := by
  sorry

/-- The supremum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `2 * 2 ^ (1 / 2)`. This is proved in
[Tao25]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 28]
theorem erdos_1038.parts.ii (n : ℕ) : 2 * 2 ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) =
    ⨆ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1} := by
  sorry

/-- The infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `< 1.835`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 28]
theorem erdos_1038.variants.inf_upperBound (n : ℕ) : ⨅ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧ f ≠ 1 ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1} < 1.835 := by
  sorry

/-- The infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `≥ 2 ^ (4 / 3) - 1`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 28]
theorem erdos_1038.varaints.inf_lowerBound (n : ℕ) : 2 ^ (4 / 3 : ℝ) - 1 ≤
    ⨅ f : {f : Polynomial ℝ // f.Monic ∧ f ≠ 1 ∧
    (f.roots.filter fun x => x ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1).card = f.natDegree},
    volume {x | |f.1.eval x| < 1} := by
  sorry

end Erdos1038

reformulations.difference: The admissible family uses a filtered real-root multiset cardinality equality, and expresses nonconstancy as f ≠ 1. The root condition is reused in all four declarations.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The filtered root multiset has cardinality at most f.roots.card, which is at most f.natDegree. Equality of the filtered cardinality with the degree therefore forces both f.roots.card = f.natDegree and the filter to retain every root. By Polynomial.splits_iff_card_roots, this is exactly splitting over ℝ with every root in [-1,1], counting multiplicities. For monic polynomials, f ≠ 1 is equivalent to positive natural degree. Both equivalences were proved independently in the scratch checks.

reformulations.difference: The supremum includes constant monic polynomials, whereas the source's family is nonconstant.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The only constant monic polynomial is 1. Its strict sublevel set {|1| < 1} is empty and has volume zero. Adding this zero value cannot change a supremum of nonnegative volumes. Equality of the two suprema, and the resulting equivalence of the equality statements, were proved in Lean.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked. The strict bound inf < 1.835 is explicitly supported by Sothanaphan's example with length between 1.8344 and 1.8345 and Tao's summary in post 2352; it is not an erroneous truncation of the overview's decimal. Boundary and elaboration checks in /workspace/review/checks.lean compile without errors and do not use the problem's sorry-backed theorems. They cover zero and constant polynomials, admissibility of X and X², exclusion of an out-of-interval root, nonempty indexing, supremum equivalence, real exponents, and the exact decimal constant. The source still records OPEN; its three recent proof submissions are explicitly unverified claims, so they do not justify a status change.
